title: Nature’s Fireworks
caption: Nebulae, the Milky Way and airglow over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Pink clouds seem to burst across the sky like fireworks over ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. They are really nebulae, large gatherings of glowing gas. The bright river of the Milky Way curves from horizon to horizon, with the Magellanic Clouds, two nearby dwarf galaxies, to its right.

On the left, a pale white column of zodiacal light rises from the horizon. It is sunlight scattered by dust in the Solar System. A green glow at the centre is airglow, created by various processes high in Earth's atmosphere.

ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek digitally projected the photograph to fit in as much sky as possible. That is why the roads leading to the 3.58-metre New Technology Telescope on the left and the 3.6-metre telescope on the right look bent. The picture also shows why observatories are built in remote, often harsh places. At La Silla, the sky is so clear and so free of artificial light that all this faint glow comes through.
scale: The source lists a distance of 10000 light years, so the light in this picture set out roughly 10,000 years ago.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape photograph by Petr Horálek, digitally projected to show as much of the sky as possible. The source gives no other camera or colour details.
understand.eye: The digital projection bends straight roads and the Milky Way into curves, so the geometry differs from what an eye would see on the spot.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: A wide, digitally projected view of the night sky with pink glowing nebulae along the Milky Way, the Magellanic Clouds to its right, a pale column of zodiacal light on the left and green airglow in the centre, above two telescopes and distorted roads.
